newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Dowd itching for action in Super 12.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Dowd itching for action in Super 12.

text.p: AUCKLAND, March 14 - All Black and Auckland Blues prop Craig Dowd is itching for action after missing out on his team's opening two Super 12 rugby matches in South Africa, NZPA reports.
Dowd was granted dispensation by the Blues management to stay at home with his wife, who was due to give birth during the Blues tour to Europe and South Africa.
Back for tonight's big game against the Waikato Chiefs at Albany, Dowd said it had been difficult watching all the action on television.
"I am eager, it has been a long time and it has been pretty hard to sit on the sidelines and watch a few games," he said.
"I have some concerns over my match fitness; I have been training but it is a completely different story when it comes to games."
Dowd said he was aware of how well the Waikato Chiefs front row of Michael Collins, Greg Smith and Richard Loe had performed so far, but added that it was up to the Blues to collar them quickly.
"I am expecting more of the same from them, but it is up to us to do our job and put our own pressure on to stop them," he said.
Dowd has also noticed the emergence of a handful of impressive young front rowers such as Collins, Auckland's Paul Thomson and Otago's Carl Hoeft and Kees Meuws, to name a few.
"Those young fellas who are coming through, one day they could be good props. Those days are coming, they are getting hardened and it is getting tougher (to dominate)," Dowd said.
